notes:
Listening tour, week 1. Hannah Liu, PLM Platform Lead, Engineering IT (my team). 60 minutes.

Hannah's team runs 3DEXPERIENCE, the legacy CAD vault, and the PLM-to-SAP interface. "We spend sixty percent of our time on break-fix and access requests." The SAP interface is a nightly batch with no alerting; failures are found by plants. Hannah has asked twice for budget to move it to event-driven integration.

The legacy CAD vault from an acquired business unit is the top risk: unsupported software, a failed cybersecurity review, and a vendor contract that ends next year. About 400 engineers still use it daily. "If that vault goes down, a business unit stops."

On requirements: requests arrive by email, Teams, and hallway, "with no way to say no or later." Hannah wants a single intake and a transparent backlog so business leaders can see trade-offs. Hannah pushed back on adding more mandatory ECO fields: "Every field we add, engineers find a way around. We need smarter defaults, not more fields."

Data quality: three part masters after the acquisitions, no common classification, no scorecard.

Team: strong on platform skills, thin on product management. Two people are at burnout risk.

Success: break-fix under 30 percent of time, and the vault retired on schedule.

Follow-up: get the cybersecurity finding report on the vault.

extraction.summary: Hannah Liu is the PLM Platform Lead in Engineering IT (on the new manager's own team), running 3DEXPERIENCE, the legacy CAD vault, and the PLM-to-SAP interface. Their top concerns are retiring the unsupported legacy CAD vault from an acquired business unit before its vendor contract ends next year, cutting break-fix load from sixty percent to under 30 percent of team time, and putting a single intake and transparent backlog in place for requests.

follow_up_questions: Can you share the cybersecurity finding report on the legacy CAD vault?
What is the exact vendor contract end date for the vault, and is there a migration plan or target system (e.g., 3DEXPERIENCE) for its ~400 users?
Why were the two budget requests for event-driven SAP integration declined, and what was the estimated cost?
How often does the nightly SAP batch fail, and what is the impact on plants when it does?
How does the sixty percent break-fix time split between break-fix and access requests, and which systems drive most of it?
Who is proposing the additional mandatory ECO fields, and what smarter defaults would you suggest?
Is there an owner or plan for consolidating the three part masters and defining a common classification?
Which two team members are at burnout risk, and what immediate relief would help them?
